doc.title: Bill Charlap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000

title: Rehearsal and preparation for recording dates
summary: Prep varies from sight-reading at the date to extensive preparation on his own records.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Right. When you get a call to play a recording date, what kind of rehearsal time?

All depends on the date. You’d have to be more specific. There are dates when I go in and we get the music right there at the date, five seconds before we play it. And you’d just better listen and have a concept of what it is musically that the group is trying to get across, or the duet, or whatever it is. Or I’ve had records where I’ve prepared extensively, where I’ve — I’m preparing less now because I’m more experienced and I’m able to walk in with many years of experience and have that as preparation. But when I’m doing my own records I’ll prepare pretty extensively.
